title: Your first air fryer: the six checks before you buy
desc: A first-time buyer's checklist: six things to compare, each one a spec you can read on the listing before you spend anything.
image_caption: Editorial illustration. Not a product photograph.
body:
Buying your first air fryer is not a research project. It is six checks, and every one of them is a line you can read on the listing itself — no reviews to decode, no "top 10" to trust. This page walks the six checks in the order that matters, using the three air fryers in this shop as worked examples. Which one is right depends on your kitchen, not on a ranking.

The six checks

#CheckHow to do it in one minuteSource
1Count the basketsA dual-basket unit (two 3-Qt baskets, B0CDY277D3) cooks a main and a side at once; a single-basket unit (B08DKYBTPH) cooks one bigger batch. Neither is better — they answer different dinners.B0CDY277D3 · B08DKYBTPH
2Match the capacity to your batchThe listings state 6 quarts (as two 3-Qt baskets), 8 quarts (single basket) and a 26-quart oven cavity (B09B7SB46R). Write down the meal you cook most and check it against the number, not the marketing.B0CDY277D3 · B08DKYBTPH · B09B7SB46R
3Measure the counter firstThe oven-style unit lists a 16.9-inch depth — measure counter depth and cabinet clearance before anything else. The basket units list roughly 13 inches.B09B7SB46R · B0CDY277D3 · B08DKYBTPH
4Weigh the storageListed weights: 13.3 lb (B0CDY277D3), 12.8 lb (B08DKYBTPH), 26.5 lb (B09B7SB46R). The last one is about double — plan where it lives when it is not in use.B0CDY277D3 · B08DKYBTPH · B09B7SB46R
5Read the functions, not the preset countOne listing's title and bullets disagree on its own preset count (24 vs 25 — FLG-015), which is a good reminder: the number is marketing. Look for the functions you will actually use weekly.B09B7SB46R
6Check price and availability on Amazon, not hereThis site does not display prices — Amazon's own policies are the reason, and the listing shows the live figure anyway.Amazon Program Policies (S02)

All product figures above are the manufacturers' own listing statements, read 2026-11-20; every row links the listing it came from. Blank or disputed values are published on Flagged for review rather than guessed.

What this page cannot tell you. No price, rating or review count appears on this site, and nobody here has cooked with these units, so no testing claim is made. The six checks are a way to read a listing critically — the decision is yours.

Shop the three units these checks were written from

CARDS
faq: What size air fryer should a first-time buyer get?

The honest answer is: the size of the meal you cook most. The listings in this shop state 6 quarts split as two 3-qt baskets, 8 quarts in one basket, and a 26-quart oven cavity. Each row on this page links the listing that states it, so you can match the number to your own tray, bird or batch of fries.
Do I need a dual-basket air fryer?

Only if you routinely cook two things that finish at the same time. The dual-basket listing names two independent 3-quart baskets with a Sync Finish; the single-basket listing is one larger basket. Both statements are the sellers' own, linked from the rows above.

The basket listings describe nonstick, dishwasher-safe baskets in their own copy. Read that wording on the listing before you buy, and remember the accessories on an oven-style unit are more parts to wash.
Why are there no prices on this page?
Amazon's Program Policies are the reason this site does not display prices; the check on every card takes you to the listing where the live figure is. See the source register (S02).
